             pyenv_version_name: false,
             pyenv_prefix: "pyenv ",
             python_binary: VecOr(vec!["python", "python3", "python2"]),
-            format: "via [${symbol}${pyenv_prefix}(${version} )(\\($virtualenv\\))]($style)",
+            format: "via [${symbol}${pyenv_prefix}(${pyenv_version} )(v${version} )(\\($virtualenv\\))]($style)",
body:
For python maybe this would be a good time to make a bigger change and deprecate the `pyenv_prefix` and `pyenv_version_name` and just use the format string with the new `pyenv_version` variable. This would simplify the code and make the configuration a bit more consistent. This would be a breaking change at the moment to use the pyenv version you would have to set the following
```toml
[python]
pyenv_version_name = true
```
after this you would need to do
```toml
[python]
format = 'via [${symbol}pyenv ${pyenv_version} (\($virtualenv\))]($style)'
```
What do you think?

body:
I'm fine with with removing the `pyenv_prefix` since I don't see any benefits to it vs. inserting its value directly in the format string since I'm always editing the format string anyway, though there might be users who are fine with the format and only need to change a prefix? No clue how common it is
Re. the `pyenv_version_name` — if it's removed would this mean that every prompt refresh would need to make calls to both python **and** pyenv to update even if the user doesn't have/use pyenv? That might be a performance issue?

Otherwise I've incorporated all the other code simplifications and will push shortly to see how this affects all those CI checks
